title: [CQ-I06] Client integration and hardening
description:
Objective: Verify client/daemon reconnects, stale approvals, packaged runtime/provider assets and cross-platform UI contracts.

Deliverable: Client integration and hardening. This is task I06 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): I05, R13, V12, C11.
definitionOfDone: Both clients consume identical daemon verdicts.
Packaged plugins contain all required production helper assets and no test fixtures.
Windows engines and certified host smoke are recorded honestly.
Fresh verification `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
CI WIRING (owed by CQ-I03a; see its hand-forward comment on this task). Edit only .github/workflows/ci.yml and report it in modifiedFiles.

Append `scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs` to the END of the explicit `node --test ...` file list in the 'Test local runner prerequisite bundles' step of job build-all-platforms (ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest). By WORKING time, CQ-R10d1, CQ-V04b1 and CQ-V04b have landed their own appended entries in that list. Read the landed line first, keep every entry and its order, and change nothing else in the workflow.

Why only this file:
- The VC-* rows use fakes only. CQ-I03a QA saw them pass on Linux Node 18-24 and Windows Node 24.16.
- CQ-I06b's tests need no CI line. moe-vscode `npm test` (tests/*.test.cjs) already runs in the same 3-OS matrix ('Test VS Code daemon startup', full checkout, so ../moe-jetbrains is present). ClientVerdictCorpusTest runs under 'Run plugin tests' in job build-plugin.
- CQ-I06c's checks ride the existing local-runner-bundle entry and 'Verify packaged JetBrains onboarding'.

Guard: scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs asserts this step with the prefix regex /run: node --test scripts\/tests\/local-runner\.test\.mjs scripts\/tests\/local-runner-bundle\.test\.mjs/. An append keeps it matching. Confirm by running that one test file.

DOCS SWEEP for the CQ-I epic, held back for this final task. Before writing, read the landed code: CQ-I03 (ManagedVmPresentation.kt, ManagedVmPanel.kt, MoeBundle.properties) and CQ-I05 (moe-vscode/src/util/ManagedVm.ts, its tree provider, package.json contributes). Claim nothing beyond them. Report all three files.

1. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md '## Plugin Bundling'. The current tree lists only moe-agent.ps1/.sh under scripts/. Replace it with what both bundles ship after CQ-I06c (JetBrains `<plugin>/`, VS Code `bundled/`):
   - daemon/ and proxy/: dist minus *.test.* and *.spec.*, plus package.json, plus node_modules minus .bin;
   - scripts/: moe-agent.ps1, moe-agent.sh, moe-call.sh, prompt-cache*.mjs, usage-*.mjs, analyze-usage.mjs, moe-account-lease.mjs;
   - scripts/local-runner/: the production modules and certified-provider.json, vm-control.mjs included; tests, specs and fixtures excluded;
   - scripts/mods/: minus *.test.ts and .claude-plugin/types;
   - docs/roles, docs/skills, docs/agent-context.md.
   Then name the guards:
   - the bundlers' required-asset lists, which fail the build;
   - the packaged checks in `node scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs <extracted bundle>`: required helpers, the packaged vm-control import closure, and no test artifacts. CI runs them on the built JetBrains zip; scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs runs them on real VS Code bundler output.
2. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md: add '### Client verification record (CQ-I)', a short table of what proves each contract, where it runs, and what is NOT certified.
   - /ws CLIENT_HELLO and approval admission: daemon vitest.
   - Approval binding plus reconnect, and managed-VM decode: the shared corpus moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-verdicts.json, run by JetBrains JUnit and VS Code node:test.
   - Packaging: the bundle test plus the onboarding packaged checks.
   - Windows engines:
     - both IDEs launch seats with Windows PowerShell 5.1 (JetBrains TerminalAgentLauncher `powershell.exe`, VS Code AgentLauncher `powershell`);
     - CI windows-latest runs the PowerShell 5.1 and 7 wrapper suites, Windows Node, and the VS Code tests;
     - JetBrains JUnit runs on ubuntu in CI.
   - Native provider smoke (`node scripts/local-runner/cli.mjs native-smoke --work-dir <abs>`): operator-invoked on real hardware, never in CI. Its per-platform state comes from CQ-R13's landed evidence, established or not established, never inferred.
   - Headless only: no IntelliJ sandbox (runIde) or VS Code Extension Host interaction is certified.
   - verified-local stays unavailable (EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY), and neither IDE offers it.
   Keep run counts, versions and dates OUT of the doc, because they rot. They go in complete_task (step 3).
3. User-facing docs for the Managed VMs surface:
   - moe-vscode/README.md: add the Managed VMs view to Features and Getting started. Add its commands to Commands with the exact titles from the landed package.json. Add one Known issues line: cleanup needs Node 22+ and a loopback daemon, and otherwise preserves every VM, including in WSL agent mode (bindHost 0.0.0.0).
   - moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.xml <description>: add one <li> for the Managed VMs tab. It covers provider readiness and reconcile/cleanup of Moe-owned VMs only, and never enables verified-local. Leave <change-notes> to the release.

VERIFY ONCE. This is the epic gate and its only full regression; run every command fresh. Never run in the shared tree, never overwrite the Windows node_modules, and clear MOE_*.

Error handling for findings:
- Edit only what a finding needs.
- Fix forward only in the owning module, at most ~20 lines, and report the file.
- Anything bigger becomes a new defect task plus report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds.
- Never weaken or skip a test.
- Before calling a red result a regression, rerun it without this epic's changes.
- Release every lease and delete every temp copy on every exit path.

A. Linux snapshot: `git archive HEAD` of the whole repo, native Linux deps, Linux-only PATH (`mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate`).
  1. `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` plus `npx tsc --noEmit`. I01 changed the /ws protocol, so this is full regression.
  2. `cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test`. Snapshot only: its pretest rebuilds dist.
  3. `cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile`. This covers I04, I05 and the I06b corpus rows.
  4. The CI local-runner step's exact file list under `env -i`, now including local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs.
  5. The packaged runtime:
     - run `npm run build` in packages/moe-daemon and packages/moe-proxy AFTER run 1, because prebuild regenerates sources;
     - run `node moe-vscode/scripts/bundle-assets.mjs`;
     - run `node scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs moe-vscode/bundled` and `node scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs`, each ending with its PASS line;
     - `find moe-vscode/bundled -path '*/node_modules' -prune -o -type f \( -name '*.test.*' -o -name '*.spec.*' -o -iname '*testharness*' \) -print` must print nothing.
  6. Root `npm run lint`.
B. Windows engines, from a Windows-side copy of the same archive, e.g. %TEMP%\moe-i06-win (`mem:gotcha-qa-windows-launcher-tests-from-wsl`).
  7. THE GATE (DoD 4). Hold the `jetbrains-gradle` lease and release it even on failure. Run `cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d <copy>\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun"`; it must exit 0. Use the build/test-results/test/TEST-*.xml timestamps and counts to show that ClientVerdictCorpusTest, PlanReviewApprovalStateTest and ManagedVmPresentationTest ran. If a POSIX JDK exists, also run the pinned `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test`. Otherwise say so, and label the evidence as the Windows equivalent.
  8. Windows Node: `node --test scripts\tests\local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs scripts\tests\local-runner-bundle.test.mjs`, and record `node --version`.
  9. The packaged wrapper parses on both engines. Take the bundled scripts\moe-agent.ps1 from run 5, copied byte-identical. Run [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile on it under `powershell.exe -NoProfile` and under `pwsh.exe -NoProfile`. Each must report 0 errors. Record both $PSVersionTable.PSVersion values.
  10. JetBrains package (DoD 2), best effort and honest. Run `.\gradlew.bat buildPlugin` in the copy; it needs a fresh daemon/proxy dist plus node_modules. Extract the zip and run `node scripts\tests\onboarding.mjs <extracted>\moe-jetbrains`; it must PASS. If that is not feasible here, state exactly why, and cite the CI step 'Verify packaged JetBrains onboarding' plus CQ-I06c's static Gradle checks. Never claim a package that was not built.
C. Host smoke record (DoD 3).
  - Run `node scripts/local-runner/cli.mjs prerequisites` with Linux node and with Windows node, and record the provider codes.
  - Do NOT run native-smoke. It is operator-invoked, launches a real VM, may download ~600 MB, and this host has no Multipass. Record it as not run.
  - Quote CQ-R13's landed per-platform certification evidence (task-f4811a72 completion and review summaries). A platform R13 did not establish is recorded as 'not certified'.

Supply to complete_task: the exact gate command (labelled as the Windows equivalent), its exit code and its output tail, plus one line per numbered run with counts and engine/version.

amendments.description:
ADVERSARIAL WHOLE-EPIC REVIEW, once, last. Load adversarial-self-review.

Read the whole CQ-I diff. Find its commits with `git log moe/work-2026-10-24 --grep 'Moe-Task: <id>'` for I01, I02, I03a, I03, I04, I05, I06a, I06d, I06b and I06c. Look for what the slices got wrong about each other.

- Producer/consumer drift:
  - vm-control schemas and codes against both decoders. A code with no specific text renders as 'unknown code <CODE>'; confirm that is consistent across both.
  - Approval revision semantics, plus error correlation: both IDEs now act only on APPROVE_TASK errors whose context.taskId is theirs, and latch on PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH.
  - CLIENT_HELLO: the daemon supports it and neither IDE sends it, by decision. Confirm the F04b token-free refusal is still actionable in both IDEs.
- Activation surface:
  - Grep both clients: no path sends executionProfile or deliveryPolicy in UPDATE_SETTINGS.
  - Neither IDE offers verified-local, and the strong profile is always blocked.
- Reconnect:
  - A disconnect while an approval is pending leaves it unconfirmed in both IDEs (corpus rows A21-A23).
  - The daemon resets per-socket negotiation on reconnect (I01 tests).
- Windows:
  - vm-control receives a project path with spaces and a drive letter as argument arrays, with no shell (JetBrains ProcessBuilder list, VS Code execFile array).
  - Note the Windows-vs-WSL ledger split.
- Packaging: no test artifacts, and every required helper is present (runs 5 and 10).
- Residuals: give each one an owning task id, or mark it 'unowned: human decision'. Search moe.search_tasks first. Known so far:
  - profile/evidence status UI (I02 note, depends on V06);
  - VS Code JSON.parse accepts lossy literals the daemon never emits;
  - cleanup preserves everything below Node 22 and when bindHost is 0.0.0.0;
  - the npm moe-proxy package ships compiled tests;
  - SettingsPanel says 'Settings saved.' when the send failed (I04 note);
  - five producer codes have no bundle text.
  File new defect tasks only for real defects. File them outside this epic unless they break DoD 1 or 2; if they do, report_blocked on them.
- Rails: no .moe edits, no Git writes, none of globalRails.forbiddenPatterns in the epic diff, verified-local untouched.

Then write the Serena memory 'task-task-4e412148225f480c8c0d5a1706a3cc76-handoff', recording the evidence per run, the owner of each residual, and what remains uncertified.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Planning CQ-I06 as a single task came to about 13 files and well over the 400-net-LOC QA cap. It was split with SPIDR on 2026-10-30, following V12a/b and C11a. CQ-I06 stays the epic's single final task (epic.finalTaskId) and now dependsOn three mid-epic slices:
- CQ-I06a (task-b20f7a40) fixes a real reconnect divergence. JetBrains ignored disconnects (PlanReviewDialog.onStatus is a no-op). A reconnect snapshot of WORKING at the rendered revision then reported success in JetBrains but 'not confirmed' in VS Code, and an AWAITING_APPROVAL snapshot wedged JetBrains in PENDING. JetBrains now adopts the VS Code recovery behaviour the human confirmed on 2026-09-11.
- CQ-I06b (task-f2d3d553) covers DoD 1: one client-neutral corpus, client-verdicts.json, stored as a JetBrains test resource and read by both IDE test suites.
- CQ-I06c (task-f18eef7a) covers DoD 2: proxy dist ships compiled *.test.js, daemon dist ships tools/toolTestHarness.js, and vm-control.mjs is not required.
Rejected:
- A JetBrains codeName fix for PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH. In-order delivery means the newer-revision frame already latched both clients, so it is a recorded residual.
- Changing the proxy tsconfig, which would lose proxy test typechecking at build. Bundler filters are used instead.
- A new docs file. DEVELOPMENT.md's Plugin Bundling section is stale anyway.
- Running native-smoke. It is operator-invoked on real hardware, and CQ-R13 owns certification.

planningNotes.risks:
- The JetBrains package build on Windows may be infeasible: npm installs, the requireFreshDist mtime guard, or network. Report it honestly rather than claim it.
- The shared tree may again hold a peer's unfinished merge (`mem:gotcha-shared-checkout-unfinished-merge`). Gate in archive snapshots only (`mem:gotcha-jetbrains-gate-snapshot`).
- I06b's VS Code tests read ../../moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-verdicts.json, so an archive of moe-vscode alone fails. Archive the whole repo.
- Proxy `npm test` deletes and rebuilds dist (pretest), so never run it in the shared tree.
- Docs must not claim certifications or engines that did not run, and must not carry counts that will rot.
- Each residual must name an owner, not just be listed.
